calvary-chapel-fredericksburg.assessment: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg checks most of the boxes Moop cares about. The leadership page shows a clear elder/pastor structure with male pastoral leadership, a dedicated Men's Ministry leader (Joe Gallegos), and a full complement of ministries including youth, children, prayer, and outreach. CC churches typically hold to Scripture inerrancy, salvation by grace through faith alone, and complementarian leadership. The charismatic-adjacent culture (CC is Spirit-friendly but not charismatic in the more extreme sense) may be a moderate fit for Moop's background. The verse-by-verse preaching model is one of the best in evangelical Christianity. Strong candidate.

calvary-fellowship-mennonite-blackville-.assessment: Calvary Fellowship Mennonite Church was established in 1968 in Blackville, South Carolina, when a group of Mennonite families from Ohio and Indiana relocated to the area. Affiliated with the Beachy Amish-Mennonite Fellowship, the church practices plain Anabaptist witness with bishop/minister/deacon polity, male-only ordination, plain dress, women's head covering, and a simple agricultural lifestyle. The congregation also operates Calvary Fellowship Mennonite School. Pastor Sam Troyer leads per 2023-2024 records. The Beachy tradition arose from a 1927 division in the Casselman River Old Order Amish in Pennsylvania, led by Bishop Moses M. Beachy — adopting evangelical outreach while maintaining plain Anabaptist conviction. Green rating.

calvary-lutheran-lcms-jacksonville-nc.assessment: Calvary Lutheran Church in Jacksonville, NC is part of the Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod — one of the most confessionally faithful Lutheran bodies in the U.S. LCMS holds inerrancy of Scripture, justification by faith alone, the bodily resurrection, male-only pastoral ordination, and a Trinitarian creedal Christology rooted in the Book of Concord. The church's "Divine Service" liturgical format (8:00 AM and 10:30 AM Sundays, with Adult Bible Study and Sunday School at 9:15 AM) is the historic Lutheran Mass — Law and Gospel preaching, Word and Sacrament. Located at 206 Pine Valley Rd and serving Marines and families from Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River, this church offers a stable, confessional alternative in a region dominated by Baptist and Methodist congregations. The pastor name is not displayed on the staff page (a link to "Meet Our Pastor" exists but content was not directly verifiable on fetch), so verify pastor on visit. Men's ministry is not visibly advertised — Lutheran congregations often run men's formation through Bible classes and Lutheran Hour Ministries rather than branded "men's ministry" — but worth asking on a visit. Strong recommendation for confessional Lutheran or liturgically-minded Christians in the Onslow County area.

cathedral-st-matthew-apostle.assessment: The Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle is DC's most historically significant Catholic church — site of President Kennedy's funeral Mass in 1963 and the Red Mass for the US Supreme Court each October. For USMC Ministries, it is important to understand this institution in the DC context, especially for Catholic veterans and their families. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the core soteriology concern is real: Roman Catholicism does not affirm justification by faith alone in Christ alone. For Catholic-background veterans, this is a place of genuine spiritual heritage. For Protestant-background men seeking Gospel clarity, the soteriology differences require honest acknowledgment. Included here for denominational context and situational awareness — DC military/government personnel will have Catholic colleagues and this cathedral represents their tradition with dignity.

cathedral-st-thomas-more-arlington.assessment: The Cathedral of St. Thomas More is the seat of the Diocese of Arlington — one of the most theologically conservative Catholic dioceses in the United States. Trinitarian orthodoxy and male-only priesthood are firmly maintained, and the 2023-2024 neogothic renovation signals liturgical seriousness. The MOOP rubric flags this red on soteriology: Roman Catholic teaching on justification (faith + works + sacraments, Council of Trent) is not Protestant sola fide. Not the right fit for faith-alone evangelicals, but for Catholics seeking reverent liturgy and orthodox moral teaching, this is a flagship parish.
